description: Remote-sensing observation is ingested
Observation causes or represents a change/state mutation
Changed observation is associated with a spatial state
Spatial dependency relationship is represented
Affected spatial dependency closure is determined
Downstream spatial states are updated
Spatial state contributes to administrative state
Multiple spatial states can contribute to one administrative state
Administrative state contributes to risk state
Multiple administrative/spatial states can contribute to one risk state
Mutation propagates through spatial -> administrative -> risk relationship
Unrelated spatial/event regions remain isolated
Shared administrative dependency is preserved correctly after mutation
Shared risk dependency is preserved correctly after mutation
Historical state/version is preserved
Previous state can be reconstructed
Dependency topology can change
Addition/removal/redirection of dependency is handled
Downstream closure is recomputed after topology mutation
Current state and historical state coexist
Observation/state lineage is retained
State change remains attributable to source observation
Multiple events/regions can coexist without accidental merging
One event/region can affect a shared downstream administrative/risk state
Changing Event/Region A does not incorrectly rewrite Event/Region B
Complete spatial -> administrative -> risk crosswalk is represented as dependency structure
Dependency structure is updated in response to observation/state mutation
Historical versions remain valid after subsequent mutations
Shared downstream state is recalculated from remaining valid upstream contributors
Complete mechanism operates as one integrated technical system
